title: Executed and imagined grasp forces recorded with stereo-EEG (Murphy et al., 2016): 4 participants, power and pinch force-matching
description: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from four adults with drug-resistant epilepsy performing force-matching tasks with a power grasp and a lateral pinch. Two participants also completed blocks in which they only imagined producing the force. Each block contained trials at three force targets (20, 30 and 40% of maximum voluntary contraction). Recordings were sampled at 2000 Hz and include the analog force signal, and were converted to BIDS from a Dryad deposit.
methods_description: SEEG was recorded with a Blackrock Neuroport amplifier at 2000 Hz alongside an analog dynamometer force signal. Participants performed power grasp and lateral pinch force-matching tasks, executed or imagined, with 5 s target presentation and 5 s rest. Event timing came from the Simulink log (SLCdata). The original NSx int16 samples were written unchanged to BrainVision format.
